steps.text: Spread the peanut butter on one side of one slice of bread. Top with sliced banana, then slices of cooked bacon. Cover with the other slice of bread. Spread butter on the outside of the sandwich.
Heat a skillet over medium heat. Fry the sandwich on each side until golden brown and peanut butter is melted, about 4 minutes total.

raw_recipe.headline: Elvis Sandwich
raw_recipe.description: This sandwich may sound unappealing, but it's actually very tasty, especially on cold winter days! Legend has it that this was a favorite of The King.
raw_recipe.name: Elvis Sandwich

review.reviewBody: I'm always up for trying new things and this really caught my attention because I'm a big fann of sweet and salty things. This was both put together. I loved every bite and it was gone in a matter of seconds. Easy to make and one of the quickest. Thanks :) I'll definitely try this one again :)
Love it, I used applewood thick cut bacon and added some dry Cajun spices
Great recipe as is. I like to use brioche for my bread because it really fries up perfectly in the skillet.
A classic of its kind. (And in a class by itself!) For a much less greasy effect, fry the sandwich unbuttered in a nonstick pan. (Do that with grilled cheese sandwiches, too!)

We followed the recipe, however on one sandwich we tried cooking the bananas in a frying pan with peanut oil before we put it on the sandwich, and we found that that was better. The bacon is optional but we thought it added something, and we prefer the sandwich with the bacon.

Today is the 2nd time I made this. The first time I made itas the recipe says but used Honey Peanut Butter (instead of drizzling the extra honey). Pretty good but needed a little something extra for my taste. So today I added a smear of plain cream cheese to the sandwich and YUM! That was the extra something it needed. It's a strange concoction and an acquired taste, but on a cold day it was really gooey & satisfying. And to my surprise, he bacon is actually good with it.

this is similiar to a sandwich we've been eating for years - but never had a name....decided to try this one...and it's good! we've made ours with apple instead of banana....on whole grain bread.... sounds weird but is delicious!
Very good. Made it last night. Only thing I changed was using whole wheat bread and no butter, cooking spray.
Always wanted to learn how to make an Elvis sandwich. Bacon was a star ingredient.

Great sandwich, me and the kids loved it. I felt it was missing something though, 95% of the way there. Not sure if it’s some honey, or a slathering of strawberry jam (or maybe I just need to put more bacon in) but I’ll try both on my next treat for the kids night.

WOW. Mind blowing recipe, I cooked these for my whole family and they loved it. I think they were just shocked I could cook! It's basically a peanut butter sandwich but way better. Obviously the 10 minute preparation time is directed at experienced cooks but trust me it's worth the wait. I added an over easy bird's egg to elevate it, and each plate was served with the sandwich, a quarter of a raw banana, and 1/2 a serving of cabbage. If you add an egg, make sure to scoop the shell pieces out with a spoon because the melted butter will be HOT. The only problem we had was that my grandmother forgot to take her insulin shot before she ate and I had told her that I had used sugar-free jelly. I also didn't tell her I added chocolate chips because I was afraid she wouldn't eat it. She ended up having an episode on her drive home and was unconscious while driving! Luckily, a truck driver saw her and nudged her car safely into a ditch. It was scary, but it's not totally the recipe's fault so it still gets five stars! Also, if your brother is vegetarian, make sure to leave off the bacon to avoid getting yelled at ha!
This was really good. However, it's heavy. So half a sandwich is plenty...personal preference
This just didn't work for me.
Oh' Elvis, you can do no wrong. This is one of my guilty pleasures!

I have been making these for years, since I had first heard about Elvis' favorite sandwich on a documentary. I'm a sandwich guy so I immediately gave it a try. Obviously there is no health benefit to this sandwich so don't be eating it everyday. It however tastes great and should be enjoyed by all peanut butter and bacon lovers.
Instead of full bacon strips, I used bacon bits. Other than that, I LOVE it!

I like all the ingredients, and indeed I ate the whole sandwich. But it didn't wow me. I think it's the warm bananas, I can never get cozy with those except with Bananas Foster. But the bacon wasn't weird with this at all, you should try it if you like all these ingredients. Thanks for the recipe!
